AirSense AI

Can a cheap sensor read the air like a lab?

Simultaneous NO₂ concentration estimation via multi-sensor Metal-Oxide (MOX) calibration.

Small, cheap and easy to fool

NO₂ is a primary indicator of combustion and vehicular exhaust. Certified reference analyzers are accurate but cost tens of thousands of dollars per station and need daily maintenance, so dense urban deployment is impossible.

Low-cost MOX sensors scale, but show non-linear response, cross-sensitivity, meteorological interference (T, RH, AH) and gradual drift and aging. A tungsten-oxide sensor aimed at NO₂ also responds to O₃, CO, hydrocarbons, T, RH and AH. Simple linear calibration fails to disentangle this.

Goal: a leakage-free ML calibration mapping simultaneous MOX and weather readings to reference NO₂(GT), plus an interactive web app.

Concentration is not an AQI. NO₂ = 112.15 µg/m³ is a physical measurement. An AQI is a dimensionless regulatory composite over several pollutants and averaging windows. This project reports NO₂ concentration with a WHO 1-hour reference band, never an AQI.

The data

UCI Air Quality Dataset (ID 360), CC BY 4.0, donated by Saverio De Vito, ENEA Italy. Five MOX sensors co-located with a certified reference analyzer on a heavily trafficked Italian roadway for over a year (De Vito et al., 2008). Raw: 9,357 hourly rows × 15 columns, 0 duplicates, 0 blank rows, 2004-03-10 18:00 to 2005-04-04 14:00, strictly hourly (9,356 consecutive steps).

Cleaning funnel

  1. 9,357 raw rows
  2. Replace -200 with NaN
  3. Drop 1,642 rows with missing NO2(GT). The target is never imputed.
  4. Drop rows where all 8 inputs are missing (full hardware outage)
  5. 7,393 clean hourly rows, 0 NaNs, 0 sentinels

Leaving -200 untreated corrupts means (raw AH mean -6.838, raw CO(GT) mean -34.208). Outliers up to 333.0 µg/m³ are kept on purpose: rush-hour peaks are real events.

Missingness (-200)

Only T has negatives (13 winter rows, min -1.9 °C).

Why UCI 360

Compared with UCI Beijing Multi-Site (~420,768 rows, 12 stations) and Kaggle India CPCB (~29,531 daily rows, unofficial provenance, high missingness). UCI 360 is peer-reviewed, CC BY 4.0, right-sized, and uniquely pairs low-cost MOX outputs with certified ground truth.

Quarantined: target leakage

The seasons and the clock

NO2(GT): mean 112.15, median 109.0, P95 198.0, P99 241.0, skew 0.574. Extreme hours exceed the WHO 1-hour guideline of 200 µg/m³. Highest monthly mean: February 157.90 µg/m³. Lowest: August 68.94 µg/m³. Diurnal peak 19:00 = 149.05, minimum 04:00 = 57.78. Hour 03:00 has only 26 observations because the reference station runs automated zero/span calibration at 3 AM.

Feature scales differ hugely (AH 0.185 to 2.181 vs PT08.S4 551 to 2775), which justifies scaling for linear models. Curved scatter (especially PT08.S3) and high inter-sensor collinearity favor non-linear tree ensembles.

The pipeline

Formulation A chosen over (B) future forecasting from lagged ground truth and (C) multi-pollutant prediction: it is true virtual-sensor calibration, avoids broken lag windows from -200 outages, and lets users enter realistic simultaneous readings. The task is concentration estimation, never forecasting.

Chronological 80/20 split with no shuffling. Training and test partitions are fixed; folds use 5-fold expanding TimeSeriesSplit. SimpleImputer(median) and StandardScaler (linear model) live inside scikit-learn Pipelines fitted only on X_train.

Train 5,914
Test 1,479

Train: Mar 2004 to Jan 2005 (5,914 rows). Test: Jan 2005 to Apr 2005, winter (1,479 rows). Handle at 80 matches the project split; other positions are illustrative only.

Chronological: the test set is the unseen future winter.

Tools: Python, Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, Seaborn, scikit-learn, Streamlit. Developed in Google Colab with Google Drive persistence, packaged for GitHub and Streamlit Community Cloud.

The models

Test RMSE: Random Forest 32.629 vs Dummy 64.879 is a 49.7% reduction, and it beats Linear Regression (36.133). Switch metric:

Train R² 0.9334 vs Test R² 0.6117: mild tree overfitting plus MOX drift plus winter distribution shift. The Dummy has a negative test R² (-0.5351) because the winter test set has a higher mean NO₂ than training (seasonal shift).

Tuned vs baseline: tuned RF improved CV RMSE (23.085 vs 23.626) and reduced overfitting (Train R² 0.9172 vs 0.9334), but baseline RF had slightly lower test RMSE (32.629 vs 32.799), so it was selected objectively.

Hyperparameters: Decision Tree max_depth=8, min_samples_leaf=10, random_state=42. Random Forest 200 trees, max_depth=12, min_samples_leaf=5. GridSearchCV: n_estimators {200,300}, max_depth {8,10,12}, min_samples_leaf {5,10,15}, max_features {'sqrt',0.8}. Gradient Boosting n_estimators=200, learning_rate=0.05, max_depth=4. Model file best_no2_model.joblib (14.5 MB), deployment archive 10.76 MB.

Random Forest feature importance

PT08.S2(NMHC) carries most of the Gini importance (0.601). Mean residual on the test set is 19.0 µg/m³ (actual minus predicted): the model under-predicts the extreme winter peaks, consistent with seasonal shift and drift. See figures 8 to 10 above.

tests/test_pipeline.py: 6 of 6 pass.

  1. Deployment artifacts exist (app.py, requirements.txt, README.md, .joblib, .json, CSVs). PASS
  2. Dataset integrity: 7,393 rows, 0 NaN, 0 sentinels. PASS
  3. Schema consistency: metadata matches the 8 feature columns. PASS
  4. Median inference: finite realistic estimate (0 to 400 µg/m³). PASS
  5. Missing-input edge case: NaN injected into feature 0, predicts cleanly. PASS
  6. App syntax compiles with zero errors. PASS

Plus a live incognito end-to-end test on Streamlit Community Cloud.

Deployment note: the Streamlit app has 8 sections: Explore (Project Overview, Dataset Information, Air Quality Analytics, Statistical Analysis, Interactive Explorer) and Machine Learning (Model Performance, NO₂ Live Estimator, Conclusion & Limits). On Python 3.14 a SimpleImputer cross-version serialization issue was solved by routing validated non-null inputs directly to the trained RF (model.named_steps["model"]) and unpinning build-heavy requirements.

The honest close

Limitations

Sensor drift and seasonal shift. Single-location 2004-2005 Italian roadside (needs local recalibration elsewhere). Single-pollutant output, no AQI. No wind speed or direction, boundary-layer height or traffic counts.

Future scope

ESP32 + MQ-series/MOX sensors + DHT22 → REST → dashboard. Adaptive online drift recalibration. Multi-pollutant and official AQI engine (CO, O₃, SO₂, PM2.5). External context features (wind, traffic).

Questions this project answers

Is this future forecasting?

No. It is simultaneous estimation.

Why exclude NOx(GT) and CO(GT)?

Reference outputs are unavailable in field deployments, and NOx(GT) leaks the target because NOx = NO + NO₂. C6H6(GT) is excluded likewise. NMHC(GT) is excluded as a reference output and 90.23% missing.

Why a chronological split?

A random split inflates R² and hides drift.

Why is PT08.S4(NO2) only r = +0.16?

Humidity and temperature cross-sensitivity, resolved by combining all sensors in a non-linear RF.

Is the output an AQI?

No. It is single-gas concentration against the WHO 1-hour band.
